rationale: Start with a broad, moderately fast gradient to locate all six compounds while limiting the risk of non-elution. The retention window and critical resolutions will guide subsequent gradient and temperature adjustments.
Injection 1 already reached the maximum CRF of 1.000. Shorten the gradient by one grid step to seek a faster fully resolved method while retaining the substantial resolution margin.

Shorten the gradient another grid step while holding temperature and endpoints fixed. The current minimum resolution of 3.47 leaves ample margin to reduce analysis time while preserving the maximum CRF.

Test a further two-minute reduction in gradient duration. The minimum resolution remains 2.68, suggesting a four-minute gradient may retain full resolution and maximum CRF while shortening the analysis.
Test the minimum gradient duration to establish the speed–resolution boundary. The first pair may fall below 1.5; if so, the four-minute gradient remains the fastest confirmed fully resolved method.

Return to the shortest fully resolved gradient and raise temperature one grid step to shorten retention. This also tests temperature selectivity for the critical first pair, which limited the two-minute gradient.

Higher temperature weakened the critical first-pair separation, so test a cooler two-minute gradient with a slightly lower endpoint to recover resolution. The final hold should still elute the last compound promptly, potentially beating the four-minute methods while maintaining maximum CRF.

Raise the endpoint one grid step to accelerate the last peak while retaining the favorable low-temperature selectivity. The first-pair resolution is close to its threshold, so this tests whether the faster method can preserve maximum CRF.

Raise the starting organic fraction one step to narrow the gradient span and test whether the gentler slope restores the marginal first-pair resolution. Keeping the higher endpoint should retain much of the last-peak time advantage over injection 7.

Shift both endpoints upward one step while preserving the gradient slope that fully resolved injection 9. This should accelerate the last peak while testing whether the first pair retains its resolution at a stronger starting composition.

Raise the starting organic fraction one step while keeping the maximum endpoint and minimum gradient duration. This tests further time savings and whether the gentler gradient maintains first-pair resolution despite reduced initial retention.

Raise temperature one step to accelerate the last peak, using the improved first-pair resolution of 1.77 as a buffer. This tests whether the current narrow gradient can preserve maximum CRF at a shorter retention time.

Increase the starting organic fraction one step to seek additional time savings at the current temperature. This tests whether narrowing the gradient still helps resolution or whether the first peaks become too weakly retained.
